title.narrative: Oxfam-Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights Initiative
Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, initiative

description.narrative: Försvara och främja SRHR för flickor, kvinnor och transpersoner.

The contribution Promoting Health and Sexual and Reproductive Rights of Maya, Garifuna and Mestizo Adult Women, Young Women, Adolescent Girls and Trans Women in Guatemala, implemented by Oxfam Intermón and eight local partner organizations, during a period of five years. The Swedish contribution to the project is SEK 76,5 million and Oxfam Intermon will contribute with approximately SEK 3,5 million. The objective of this project is to defend and promote the sexual and reproductive health and rights of girls, women and trans persons in 10 regions in Guatemala. Financially, the Swedish funds allocated to this contribution will be used for the carrying out of trainings on sexual and reproductive rights with girls and women; attention and the creation of platforms where organizations of women can meet and discuss common challenges and solutions; the provision of psychosocial care to survivors of sexual violence; to provide legal assistance and accompaniment in cases of sexual violence; and other activities. Additionally, the funds also target young men who have the potential to change the social imaginary and prevent violence against women. This will be achieved through training possesses and through working with young male leaders from grassroot organizations who will, in turn, be able to affect and provide training to other young men. The activities will be implemented by the eight partner organizations and are estimated to benefit a total of more than 62 000 persons, the majority of whom are women. In addition, the project includes advocacy and awareness raising in order to affect institutions and operators working with justice, health and education on SRHR.

The Programme aims to contribute to the full exercise of sexual and reproductive health and rights for women, youth, and adolescent girls, mainly indigenous and rural to overcome patriarchal discrimination, exclusion and racism and have the opportunity to dignify their lives by addressing gender based cycles of violence and exercising their rights to health and sexual and reproductive rights.
Specific objcetives:
(i) to defend and promote sexual and reproductive health and rights of girls, women and trans persons in ten regions in Guatemala. (ii) To provide legal assistance, psychosocial care to survivors of violence and sexual violence; this will be achieved through training processes and through working with young male leaders from grass-root organizations.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
During 2024, 11 women's civil society organizations implemented strategic actions seeking to contribute to creation of more favorable contexts for women and trans women in Guatemala, helping them get out of situations of violence, increase opportunities for political and civic participation, and help them raise their voices before decision-makers in order to position women in their intersectionality. The program has evolved and adapted over the years of implementation, according to changing country contexts, lessons learnt and best practises. Year 2024 continued to be challenging without considerable changes in the situation of violence against women, young women, LGBTIQ and indigenous peoples.
In 2024, the Reproductive Health Observatory OSAR reported 56,568 births in adolescent girls; 1,953 in girls aged 10 to 14 years of age, a direct consequence of sexual violence and lack of integral sexual education. 70% of births reported the father of the new born, leaving 30% of births with single mothers. 37% of new parents were between the ages of 14-19. Nearly 40% of girls and adolescent girls suffer sexual violence between the ages of 14-19. As to violence against Trans women, there was a reported 12.5% increase in 2024 in transfemicides.
In this context, Oxfam reports some relevant results achieved in 2024, including the following:
- 400 women and young women and 70 trans women have been trained in sexual and reproductive health rights in safe spaces in 30 municipalities of 14 departments. These trainings have been carried out in local languages using culturally appropriate, feminist popular education methodologies. The 8 training modules have been validated jointly by the historic, feminist women's organizations implementing the training. The training is provided during 8-10 in situ sessions of 16-30 women. Learning is verified through pre and post questionnaires
- 85 indigenous women leaders, midwives and trans women trained as multipliers on sexual and reproductive health rights in their communities
- 50 midwives trained as women's rights defenders and in recognizing sexual violence in their professional activities at individual and community level
In 2024, 240 youth were trained as Agents of Change to carry out replicates in their communities to other youths on SRHR, violence prevention, prevention of teen pregnancies and forced marriages, and to promote preparation of Life Plans for youth. The activities included informative events, dialogues among youth groups, information kiosks and digital campaigns. Additionally, 70 teachers participated in sensitizing activities on gender equality, violence prevention and SRHR, in order to promote inclusion of these issues in classrooms.
- 54,500 people from general public received information and participated in activities regarding SRHR
- 7 communication campaigns to support women's voices and concerns were carried out; 150,000 people were reached with these campaigns
Another action line of the program was psychological support to survivors of sexual violence, within the framework of comprehensive sexual health care. This support has included individual and group therapies, emotional and psychosocial support based on Mayan cosmovision.
- In 7 departments 1,200 women and young women had access to quality sexual and reproductive health services provided by 3 Oxfam partner organizations, with access to medical attention, family planning methods, pre and post natal check ups, prevention and treatment of sexually transmitted diseases, among other services
- 1,000 trans women received specialized medical attention provided by OTRANS
- 280 women were assisted in placing criminal complaints in cases of sexual violence
The Consortium gained recognition as a relevant political actor in favor of women's and SRHR in national and international arena. One of the major positive results was the its participation in the election of the new Presidential Secretary and Sub-secretary for Women (SEPREM), and participation in the construction of SEPREM work plan for 2025. The Consortium developed a Sustainability Plan seeking to maintain the Consortium operative beyond the Sida program, including plans for seeking self sustainability of the member organizations and the Consortium as such.
The collective work of the Consortium contributed to a regional investigation "Breaking Forms" which demonstrates the link between violence against women and gender inequalities, and the construction of the law initiative 6430 to prevent child sexual abuse, participation in the 54th General Assembly of the OAS in Paraguay and in the 5th regional conference of CEPAL to tackle Montevideo Consensus at its 10 year celebration.
Finally, organizational strengthening of the 11 partner organizations has produced more robust and professional organizations, capable of administering donor funds with increased responsibility.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
